course_name_original: Fundamentos físicos de la ingeniería i

learning_outcomes.text: Correctly applies basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism to solve engineering problems.
Verifies through experimentation and group work in the laboratory the theoretical fundamentals explained in the classroom.

Knows the basic fundamentals of vector calculus. Understands the theory of Newtonian mechanics. Applies vector calculus concepts to solve problems in Newtonian mechanics and rigid body dynamics. States the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics and explains their physical implications. Identifies the theoretical fundamentals applied to problem-solving.
Facilitates the positive management of differences, disagreements, and conflicts that arise in the team.

Takes into account the views of others and provides constructive feedback. Identifies the collective goals of the group with their own. Contributes to the establishment and application of team work processes. Through their communication and interaction style, contributes to group cohesion.

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Carries out their individual contribution within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group rules. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

syllabus_topics: Vectors: Operations with vectors. Reduction of vector systems. Torsor.
Forces: Introduction. Types. Principle of action and reaction.
Particle statics. Point equilibrium: Introduction. Study of forces in the plane. Particle statics.

Systems of forces and moments: Introduction. Principle of transmissibility. Moment of a force with respect to a point. Moment of a force with respect to an axis. Moment of a couple. Reduction of a system of forces to a force and a couple. Equivalent systems.
Rigid body equilibrium: Introduction. Free body diagram. Equilibrium in the plane. Bodies subjected to distributed loads. Statically indeterminate bodies. Equilibrium in three dimensions.

Particle kinematics: Rectilinear motion. Motion of several particles. Relative motion. Holonomic motions. Curvilinear motion. Tangential and normal components of acceleration. Polar and cylindrical coordinates.

Particle kinetics: Newton's Laws. Linear momentum of a particle. Dynamic equilibrium. Angular momentum of a particle. Motion under the action of a central force. Conservation of angular momentum. Newton's Law of Gravitation.

Work and energy: Work of a force. Kinetic energy. Work-energy theorem. Application of the work-energy theorem. Power and Efficiency. Potential energy. Conservative forces. Conservation of energy. Motion under the action of a conservative central force. Linear momentum theorem. Impulsive motion. Collisions.

Systems of particles: Application of Newton's Laws to a system of particles. Linear and angular moments of a system of particles. Motion of the center of mass of a system of particles. Angular momentum of a system of particles with respect to its center of mass. Conservation of linear and angular moments in a system of particles. Kinetic energy of a system of particles. Work-energy theorem. Conservation of energy in a system of particles. Linear momentum theorem for a system of particles. Angular momentum theorem. Variable mass systems. Stationary particle flow. Systems that gain or lose mass.
assessment_rules: It is an essential condition, though not sufficient, to pass the subject to have completed and approved the laboratory practicals. In the 2nd sitting, the laboratory grade (20%) will be maintained, and a written exam covering all topics of the course (80%) will be administered.
